Read Feeding Station Export Files

Source: R/read_station.R
read_station.Rd

Read one or more NEDAP or FIRE exports (CSV, TXT or Excel), map their columns to the standard fields with a station format, and combine them into one standard table for prep_visits().

read_station(
  files,
  station = NULL,
  format = NULL,
  pattern = "\\.(csv|txt|xlsx|xls)$",
  sheet = 1,
  verbose = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

files

Character vector of file paths, or a single folder. For a folder, all files matching pattern are read.

station

"nedap", "fire" or NULL (default). With NULL, the station type is detected by trying the built-in formats on the column names. Required when format is given.

format

NULL (default) for the built-in format of station, or a station format: the path of a tab-separated format file, or a data frame with columns field, column and optionally unit (see station_format()).

pattern

Regular expression for file names when files is a folder. Default: CSV, TXT, XLSX and XLS files (case-insensitive).

sheet

Sheet name or number for Excel files. Default 1.

verbose

0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details per file).

...

Further arguments passed to data.table::fread() (CSV and TXT files).

Value

A data.table with the standard fields of the station type (see station_format()) plus source_file (file name without folder):

  • responder (character, transponder number as recorded), location (character), breed (character, if mapped);

  • entry_time, exit_time: POSIXct, clock time stored as UTC;

  • duration: seconds; feed_intake, trough_in, trough_out, topup: g; weight: kg.

Fields the station type does not have, or optional fields missing in the export, are NA. Columns of the export that are not mapped are dropped. Attribute "station" holds the station type and "station_format" the format used.

Details

CSV and TXT files are read with data.table::fread(), which detects the separator (comma, tab, semicolon). Excel files need the readxl package. The column mapped to responder is always read as text, so leading zeros are kept.

Columns are matched by name first (exact, then ignoring case and surrounding spaces). A number in the format is a column position, used when the export has no usable header. Positions are fragile: if the export software adds a column, every later field shifts without an error. Use names where possible.

Every file must contain all required fields of the station type. A missing optional field (topup, breed) is filled with NA.

See also

station_format() for the fields and the format file; prep_visits() for the next step.

Examples

# Write the example data to two CSV files, then read them back
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "fire_export")
dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 101, ], file.path(folder, "fire_101.csv"))
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 102, ], file.path(folder, "fire_102.csv"))

raw <- read_station(folder)
#> 
#> ── Reading 2 files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ Detected station type "fire"
#> ✔ Read 9794 rows from 2 files (FIRE)
head(raw)
#>    responder location          entry_time           exit_time duration
#>       <char>   <char>              <POSc>              <POSc>    <num>
#> 1:     35877      101 2023-12-19 14:15:39 2023-12-19 14:18:02       NA
#> 2:     35873      101 2023-12-19 14:18:03 2023-12-19 14:23:05       NA
#> 3:     35878      101 2023-12-19 14:23:15 2023-12-19 14:28:45       NA
#> 4:     35855      101 2023-12-19 14:29:05 2023-12-19 14:34:29       NA
#> 5:     35877      101 2023-12-19 14:34:30 2023-12-19 14:34:37       NA
#> 6:     35853      101 2023-12-19 14:34:38 2023-12-19 14:36:26       NA
#>    feed_intake weight trough_in trough_out topup  source_file
#>          <num>  <num>     <num>      <num> <num>       <char>
#> 1:          46   67.6       678        632   286 fire_101.csv
#> 2:         248   60.8       632        384     0 fire_101.csv
#> 3:         201   70.8       670        469   286 fire_101.csv
#> 4:         121   51.2       755        634   286 fire_101.csv
#> 5:           0    0.0       634        634     0 fire_101.csv
#> 6:           0   88.6       634        634     0 fire_101.csv
attr(raw, "station")
#> [1] "fire"

# The built-in format, written as a template for other exports
station_format("fire", file = file.path(folder, "fire_format.txt"))
#> ✔ Station format written to /tmp/Rtmp2HiUE2/fire_export/fire_format.txt

unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
